card.statement:
[{see <<cite:Ara07>> for the details}] As in the case of $\bar C(\fing)$, $C(\mf{g})$ is also bigraded, we can also write $\ad Q = d_++d_-$ such that $d_+(C^{i,j})\subset C^{i+1, j}, d_-(C^{i,j})\subset C^{i, j+1}$ and get a spectral sequence

$$E_r \Longrightarrow H^\bullet(C(\mf{g}), \ad Q)$$

such that

\begin{align*}
E_2^{p,q}=H^p(H^q(C(\mf{g}), d_-), d_+) \cong
\delta_{q,0} H^p(\mf{n}, U(\mf{g})\otimes_{U(\mf{n})}\C_{\chi})\\
\cong \delta_{p,0}\delta_{q,0}H^0(\finn,U(\fing)\*_{U(\finn)}\C_{\chi})\cong \End_{U(\mf{g})}(U(\mf{g})\otimes_{U(\mf{n})} \C_{\chi})^{op}.
\end{align*}

Where $\C_\chi$ is the one-dimensional representation of $\mf{n}$ defined by the character $\chi$. Thus we get the Whittaker model isomorphism <<cite:Kos78>>

$$\mc{Z}(\mf{g})\cong  H^0(C(\mf{g}), \ad Q ) \cong
\End_{U(\mf{g})}(U(\mf{g})\otimes_{U(\mf{n})} \C_{\chi})^{op}.$$
card.label: Remark 18
